_note:
The filter solves min ||u - u_mppi||^2_W + rho 1's subject to the same second-order rows, the 700 N azimuth disc and the speed-dependent bow cap, with W = diag(1/s0^2), solved in the dimensionless step v = (u - u_mppi)/s0 with each row scaled to unit coefficient norm.  The chance variant tightens each row by z sqrt(a Sigma_d a^T) with a in TAU coordinates (the disturbance is a force and does not pass through the thruster allocation); Sigma_d is diag(s_F^2) for the coloured gust and diag((s_F sqrt(2 tau_c/h))^2) for white force noise, a factor sqrt(10) larger at tau_c = 5 s, h = 1 s.
FOUR CAVEATS BELONG WITH THESE NUMBERS.  (1) The white tightening bounds the INTERVAL-AVERAGED barrier condition, not the supremum of psi1 inside the interval, while the collision statistics are evaluated at every 0.25 s sub-step.  (2) delta is per row: with four circles active a union bound gives up to 4 delta = 0.012 per instant, not 0.003.  (3) The filter solves its three-variable problem exactly while the sampler uses the closed form, which experiment V0 measured to be exact on single-row instances (4234 of 6986 active instances) and 14 % more conservative on average on two-row ones (2752 of 6986); a filter margin smaller than that is inconclusive.  (4) The inner MPPI is not told its output was filtered, so its warm start is the unfiltered plan -- the standard cascade, and this one works against the filter.
The timing in _timing was measured in the parent process while nothing else of this run was active, but each controller was driven along its OWN trajectory, so it shares the confound of the shipped V5 measurement.  See tests/timing_matched.py for the operating-point-matched version.
